# Adjudication Task — Chapter 315

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃315화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|저벅, 저벅.
  6|
  7|종남일룡 혁소평의 발걸음은 빠르지도, 느리지도 않았다.
  8|
  9|그가 걸음을 내디딜 때마다 사람들의 시선과 수군거림이 따라붙었다.
 10|
 11|“쯧쯧, 대낮부터 이런 난동을 피우다니.”
 12|
 13|“문파 제일의 후기지수라는 자가 저 모양이니, 종남파 수준도 알 만해. 이러니 화산파가 늘 섬서 제일인 게지.”
 14|
 15|“볼은 왜 저렇게 부어 있대? 듣자 하니 화산일학이 왔다던데, 혹시…….”
 16|
 17|혁소평은 자신도 모르게 뺨을 문질렀다.
 18|
 19|욱신거리는 통증은 사람들의 따가운 시선 때문만이 아니다. 무기력하게 얻어맞은 세 대의 따귀. 그리고 한 사람의 가라앉은 목소리가 생생하게 떠올랐다.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘말했던 것 같은데. 그 검, 잘 생각하고 휘두르라고.’
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|화왕 적천강이 선택한 열화문의 후인, 산서성이라는 작은 개천에서 몸을 일으킨 잠룡(潛龍).
 28|
 29|놈에 관한 이야기는 이미 지긋지긋할 정도로 들었다.
 30|
 31|하지만…….
 32|
 33|‘어떻게 그리 강할 수 있지?’
 34|
 35|도무지 이해할 수 없었다. 종남파 장문인의 적전제자로 들어가 전폭적인 지원 아래 무공을 익힌 그다.
 36|
 37|수많은 절정 무공과 영약, 십봉룡이라는 이름도 혁소평에게는 당연한 것이었다.
 38|
 39|그러나 지금, 혁소평을 둘러싼 것들이 위태롭게 흔들리고 있었다.
 40|
 41|입구에서 맞닥트린 서안루 총관의 차가운 표정은 그 증거 중 하나였다.
 42|
 43|“또 난동을 피우셨다고 들었습니다.”
 44|
 45|“난동? 약간 소란이 있긴 했지. 별일 아니니 넘어가자고.”
 46|
 47|그대로 지나치려는 혁소평의 발걸음은 다음 순간 들려온 총관의 말에 우뚝 멈췄다.
 48|
 49|“지난번에 말씀드렸었지요. 다시 한번 이런 일이 일어난다면 종남파에 정식으로 항의하겠다고요.”
 50|
 51|“항의?”
 52|
 53|번들거리는 눈빛으로 총관을 노려보던 혁소평이 입을 열었다.
 54|
 55|“우리 송 총관, 많이 컸네.”
 56|
 57|“혁 소협!”
 58|
 59|“건방 떨지 마.”
 60|
 61|혁소평의 잇새로 으르렁거리는 소리가 흘러나왔다.
 62|
 63|“루주 자식놈을 화산파 속가로 넣었다고 어깨가 올라간 모양인데…… 대종남파가 그리 우습게 보이나?”
 64|
 65|“말씀이 과하시군요.”
 66|
 67|총관의 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴에 혁소평이 입매를 비틀었다.
 68|
 69|“과한 건 네놈들이야. 술이나 파는 놈들이 감히 본문을 우습게 보다니, 간이 배 밖으로 튀어나와도 유분수지.”
 70|
 71|“그 말씀, 루주께 그대로 전해 드려도 되겠습니까?”
 72|
 73|“잊지 말고 꼭 전해. 그럼 다음에 또 보자고.”
 74|
 75|툭툭.
 76|
 77|총관의 어깨를 두드리고 걸음을 옮기는 혁소평의 입가에는 씁쓸한 웃음이 맺혀 있었다.
 78|
 79|‘이제는 하다 하다 이런 놈들에게까지 무시받을 줄이야.’
 80|
 81|물론 서안루주는 일개 장사치라고 하기에는 그 영향력이 상당했다. 섬서성의 성도인 서안. 바로 그 서안의 유흥가를 주무르는 큰손이니까.
 82|
 83|그러나 제아무리 상계(商界)의 실력자라고 해도 구파일방의 이름 앞에서는 태양 앞의 잔딧불에 불과하다.
 84|
 85|더군다나 루주도 아닌, 일개 주루의 총관에게 자신이 이런 수모를 당할 줄이야.
 86|
 87|‘갈수록 점입가경이로군.’
 88|
 89|불과 일이 년 사이 종남파의 위상은 추락을 거듭했다.
 90|
 91|그 효시(嚆矢)를 쏘아 올린 것은 수많은 이들이 지켜보는 앞에서 노호검객을 박살 낸 화왕 적천강이었고, 은거를 깬 검성 매종학과 화산신룡이라는 이름이 뒤를 이었다.
 92|
 93|어찌 한 산에 두 마리 호랑이가 있을 수 있겠는가.
 94|
 95|누군가는 강자가 되어야 하고, 누군가는 약자가 되어야 한다. 종남파의 역할은 후자였다.
 96|
 97|‘언제까지고 지금 같지는 않을 것이다.’
 98|
 99|주르륵.
100|
101|있는 힘껏 움켜쥔 주먹에서 핏줄기가 흘렀다.
102|
103|지난밤부터 쌓여 있던 주독(酒毒)은 몰아낸 지 오래. 혁소평이 굳은 얼굴로 하늘을 바라보던 그때였다.
104|
105|“헉, 허억. 대사형, 여기 계셨군요.”
106|
107|“넌…… 봉수가 아니냐?”
108|
109|혁소평이 뜻밖이라는 눈빛으로 낯익은 얼굴을 바라봤다.
110|
111|거친 숨을 몰아쉬는 청년. 그는 혁소평과 같은 종남파의 제자로, 비록 사부는 다르나 항렬은 같았다.
112|
113|“본산에 있어야 할 네가 여기에는 어쩐 일이지?”
114|
115|본산이란 서안에서 이틀 거리에 있는 종남산을 일컬었다. 봉수라 불린 혁소평의 사제가 대답했다.
116|
117|“임무 수행 중입니다. 저뿐만 아니라 태을검대(太乙劍隊) 모두가 왔지요.”
118|
119|“임무? 거기에 태을검대까지?”
120|
121|태을검대는 종남파의 이대 제자들로 이루어진 무력 집단. 비록 화산의 매화검수에 비할 바는 아니나, 종남파가 자랑하는 정예들이었다.
122|
123|어지간해서는 본산도 벗어나지 않는 태을검대가 예까지 오다니.
124|
125|혁소평이 의문으로 미간을 찡그린 그때, 사제가 입을 열었다.
126|
127|“대사형을 모셔오라는 명을 받고 왔습니다.”
128|
129|“명이라니. 누가 나를 찾는다는 말이냐?”
130|
131|“사백(師伯)께서 지금 서안에 계십니다.”
132|
133|“……!”
134|
135|혁소평이 눈을 크게 떴다. 자신과 같은 항렬인 사제가 사백이라고 부를 만한 사람은 단 두 명뿐이다.
136|
137|그중 한 사람인 노호검객 송일은 화왕에게 입은 내상으로 인해 본산에서도 두문불출하고 있으니 남은 것은 한 명뿐이었다.
138|
139|‘그런데 그분이 어째서 서안에…….’
140|
141|혁소평은 머릿속에 떠오르는 의문을 황급히 지웠다.
142|
143|둘째 사백이 자신을 찾는다면 한시도 지체해서는 안 된다. 그는 혁소평에게 있어 사부인 풍운검군보다 두려워하는 사람이니까.
144|
145|아니, 비단 혁소평뿐만 아니라 종남파의 제자 모두가 마찬가지다. 초조한 사제의 낯빛이 바로 그 증거였다.
146|
147|“대사형, 시간이 없습니다.”
148|
149|“어서 사백께 안내하거라.”
150|
151|잠시 후, 경신법을 발휘하여 빠른 속도로 쏘아지는 혁소평의 뇌리에는 한 가지 의문이 맴돌고 있었다.
152|
153|‘도대체 무슨 일이지?’
154|
155|하나는 확실했다.
156|
157|둘째 사백, 태을무정검(太乙無情劍)이 나섰다면 결코 호락호락한 일이 아니라는 것 말이다.
158|
159|
160|
161|* * *
162|
163|
164|
165|진기도인(眞氣導引)은 위험하면서도 어려운 작업이다.
166|
167|혼자 운기조식을 하더라도 주화입마의 위험은 늘 존재하는 법. 진기도인은 타인의 기운을 이끌어 운기를 해야 하니 그 어려움이야 더 말할 필요가 없다.
168|
169|‘심지어 그 대상이 화왕이라니.’
170|
171|평화 길드원들을 상대로 진기도인 할 때와는 차원이 다른 긴장감.
172|
173|나는 살얼음판에 발을 내딛는 기분으로 열양지기를 움직이기 시작했다.
174|
175|‘천천히. 조심스럽게.’
176|
177|그 두 가지만 끊임없이 되뇌었다. 일체의 잡념도 허락하지 않고 적천강의 거대한 기운을 끌어당겼다.
178|
179|후우웅.
180|
181|이내 맞닿은 두 개의 기운.
182|
183|그러나 평화 길드원들을 대할 때와 같은 충돌이나 거부감은 없었다. 그저 자연스럽게 섞여들 뿐이다.
184|
185|마치 처음부터 한 몸이었던 것처럼, 오래전 헤어진 쌍둥이를 만난 것처럼 당연하게 동화되고 이끌린다.
186|
187|‘같은 뿌리에서 자랐으니까.’
188|
189|맞다. 적천강과 나는 열화문이라는 뿌리를 공유한다.
190|
191|만약 열화신공을 익히지 않은 누군가가 섣부르게 진기도인을 시도했다면, 적천강의 막대한 공력을 감당하지 못하고 주화입마에 빠졌을지도 모른다.
192|
193|‘천만다행이지.’
194|
195|이미 몇 차례나 해 왔던 일이지만 이건 항상 무섭더라.
196|
197|나는 심장이 쫄깃해지는 것을 느끼며 본격적인 진기도인을 시작했다.
198|
199|열화신공의 구결에 따라, 이제는 하나가 된 극양(極陽)의 기운을 쉼 없이 운기했다.
200|
201|한 시진, 혹은 두 시진.
202|
203|시간의 흐름도 잊은 채 몰두하기를 한참. 영원히 끝나지 않을 것 같던 진기도인은 모든 공력이 단전에 돌아감으로써 끝이 났다.
204|
205|띠링.
206|
207|
208|
209|- [진기도인(眞氣導引)]을 성공적으로 완료했습니다!
210|
211|- 시전 대상의 병세가 미약하게 완화되었습니다!
212|
213|- 당신이 지닌 [열양지기]가 미약하게 상승합니다!
214|
215|
216|
217|“후우…….”
218|
219|눈을 감은 채 호흡을 가다듬었다.
220|
221|아직 모든 것이 끝난 것은 아니다. 나는 한순간이나마 화왕 적천강이라는 초절정 고수가 지닌 거대한 기운과 동화되었고, 하나가 되어 느꼈다.
222|
223|열화문이라는 뿌리, 그 위로 자라난 거목의 몸통과 수많은 나뭇가지들. 까마득한 경지의 일면을 똑똑히 목격했다.
224|
225|깨달음은 이런 경험과 상황 속에서 찾아오는 법이다.
226|
227|바로 지금처럼.
228|
229|‘이제야 좀 가닥이 잡히네.’
230|
231|보였다. 더 높은 경지로 가는 계단이.
232|
233|그건 누가 알려 주어서는 알 수 없는 작은 깨달음이었다.
234|
235|띠링.
236|
237|
238|
239|- [열화신공(烈火神功)]의 경지가 칠 성으로 상승했습니다!
240|
241|- 기의 운용과 수발이 더 자유로워집니다!
242|
243|- [열화문]의 무공을 한층 더 강력하고 효과적으로 펼칠 수 있습니다!
244|
245|- 깨달음의 보상으로 대량의 경험치와 보너스 포인트를 획득했습니다!
246|
247|- 레벨 업!
248|
249|
250|
251|그래, 이거지.
252|
253|나는 경쾌한 종소리와 함께 눈을 떴다. 고작 한 걸음 올라섰을 뿐인데 그 차이는 컸다.
254|
255|한층 더 날카로워진 감각들 사이로 나를 둘러싼 모든 것들에 대한 정보가 속속들이 밀려온다.
256|
257|흠뻑 젖은 전신, 배출해 낸 탁기에서 흘러나오는 악취. 그리고 등 뒤에서 소리 없이 발버둥 치는 누군가의 인기척까지.
258|
259|“…….”
260|
261|뭐여, 시벌.
262|
263|고개를 돌리자 혁무진의 전신을 아나콘다처럼 칭칭 감고 있는 청풍이 보인다. 입과 코를 야무지게 틀어막은 두 손도.
264|
265|“거기서 뭐 합니까?”
266|
267|청풍이 해맑게 대답했다.
268|
269|“혁 소협이 코골이를 하려고 해서 막고 있었어요!”
270|
271|“아, 잘했습니다. 저 새끼 때문에 열 받아서 주화입마 올 뻔했네.”
272|
273|혁무진 저 자식은 호법을 서라니까 호접지몽만 꾸고 있어.
274|
275|나는 얼굴이 파랗게 질린 채 발버둥 치는 혁무진을 바라보다가 문득 물었다.
276|
277|“코만 막으면 되지, 왜 입까지 막았어요?”
278|
279|“코를 막으니까 입에서도 소리가 나서요!”
280|
281|“아.”
282|
283|“그래서 그냥 둘 다 막았어요!”
284|
285|“음, 그럼 질식으로 죽지 않을까?”
286|
287|“귀식대법(龜息大法)을 쓰면 돼요!”
288|
289|“그 얼어 죽을 귀식대법이 정확히 뭔데.”
290|
291|“호흡을 참고, 심장 박동을 정지시키는 동시에 체온을 하강하면 돼요!”
292|
293|“끝내주네. 그런 게 가능합니까?”
294|
295|“그럼요. 지금 혁 소협이 하는 게 귀식대법이에요!”
296|
297|“무진이가?”
298|
299|“네! 이미 심장 박동이 멎었어요.”
300|
301|“……?”
302|
303|순간 뇌 정지가 온 나는 말 없이 혁무진을 바라봤다.
304|

The first shot had been fired by the Fire King Jeok Cheongang when he crushed the Roaring Fury Swordsman in front of countless witnesses. Then came the Sword Saint Mae Jonghak’s return from seclusion, followed by the name Huashan Divine Dragon.

[P44]
How could two tigers live on the same mountain?

[P45]
One had to be the strong one, and the other the weak.

[P46]
The Zhongnan Sect had been forced into the latter role.

[P47]
*It won’t always be like this.*

[P48]
Blood trickled from Hyuk Sopyung’s tightly clenched fist.

[P49]
He had expelled the last of the previous night’s alcohol from his body long ago. He was staring up at the sky with a grim expression when—

[P50]
“Gasp, gasp. Senior Brother, there you are.”

[P51]
“You’re… Bong-su?”

[P52]
Hyuk Sopyung looked at the familiar face in surprise.

[P53]
The young man was panting heavily. Like Hyuk Sopyung, he was a Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect. Though they had different Masters, they belonged to the same generation.

[P54]
“What brings you here when you should be at the main sect?”

[P55]
The main sect stood on Mount Zhongnan, two days from Xi’an. Bong-su, Hyuk Sopyung’s Junior Brother, answered.

[P56]
“I’m carrying out a mission. The entire Taeeul Sword Unit came with me.”

[P57]
“A mission? The Taeeul Sword Unit too?”

[P58]
The Taeeul Sword Unit was a fighting force composed of the Zhongnan Sect’s second-generation Disciples. Though they couldn’t compare to Huashan’s Plum Blossom Swordsmen, they were still an elite unit the Zhongnan Sect took great pride in.

[P59]
For the Taeeul Sword Unit, who rarely even left the main sect, to come all the way here…

[P60]
Hyuk Sopyung frowned in puzzlement. His Junior Brother spoke.

[P61]
“I was ordered to bring you back, Senior Brother.”

[P62]
“Ordered? Who’s looking for me?”

[P63]
“Senior Martial Uncle is in Xi’an.”

[P64]
“……!”

[P65]
Hyuk Sopyung’s eyes widened. There were only two people whom a Disciple of their generation could call Senior Martial Uncle.

[P66]
One of them, the Roaring Fury Swordsman Song Il, had shut himself away at the main sect because of the internal injury he had suffered at the Fire King’s hands. That left only one person.

[P67]
*But why is he in Xi’an…?*

[P68]
Hyuk Sopyung hurriedly pushed the question from his mind.

[P69]
If his Second Martial Uncle was looking for him, he couldn’t afford to delay for even a moment. Hyuk Sopyung feared the man more than he feared his own Master, the Wind-and-Cloud Sword Lord.

[P70]
And it wasn’t only Hyuk Sopyung. Every Disciple of the Zhongnan Sect felt the same way.

[P71]
The anxiety on his Junior Brother’s face was proof enough.

[P72]
“Senior Brother, there’s no time.”

[P73]
“Take me to Senior Martial Uncle at once.”

[P74]
A short while later, Hyuk Sopyung shot forward at tremendous speed using his movement technique. One question kept circling through his mind.

[P75]
*What on earth is going on?*

[P76]
One thing was certain.

[P77]
If his Second Martial Uncle, the Taeeul Merciless Sword, had stepped in, this was no ordinary matter.

[P78]
* * *

[P79]
True Qi Guidance was a dangerous and difficult undertaking.

[P80]
Even when circulating one’s qi alone, there was always a risk of qi deviation. True Qi Guidance required circulating someone else’s qi for them, so its difficulty needed no explanation.

[P81]
*Especially when that someone is the Fire King.*

[P82]
The tension was on an entirely different level from when I had performed True Qi Guidance on the Peace Guild members.

[P83]
Feeling as though I were stepping onto thin ice, I began moving the Scorching Yang Qi.

[P84]
*Slowly. Carefully.*

[P85]
I repeated those two words over and over. Allowing myself no distracting thoughts, I drew in Jeok Cheongang’s immense qi.

[P86]
Whoooong.

[P87]
The two streams of qi met.

[P88]
But there was none of the collision or resistance I had encountered with the Peace Guild members. They simply blended together.

[P89]
They merged and yielded to my guidance as though they had always been one—as naturally as twins reuniting after a long separation.

[P90]
*Because they grew from the same root.*

[P91]
That was right. Jeok Cheongang and I shared the same root: the Fire Gate Clan.

[P92]
If someone who hadn’t learned the Fire Gate Divine Technique had rashly attempted True Qi Guidance, they might have failed to withstand Jeok Cheongang’s immense internal energy and fallen into qi deviation.

[P93]
*What a relief.*

[P94]
I had already done this several times, but it never stopped being terrifying.

[P95]
With my heart in my throat, I began the True Qi Guidance in earnest.

[P96]
Following the formula of the Fire Gate Divine Technique, I ceaselessly circulated the Extreme Yang qi that had now become one.

[P97]
One shichen, or perhaps two.

[P98]
I lost all sense of time in my concentration. The True Qi Guidance, which had seemed as though it would never end, finally came to a close when all the internal energy returned to the dantian.

[P99]
Chime.

[P100]
> **System**
> - **True Qi Guidance** successfully completed!
> - The target’s condition has improved slightly!
> - Your **Scorching Yang Qi** has increased slightly!

[P101]
“Phew…”

[P102]
I closed my eyes and steadied my breathing.

[P103]
It wasn’t over yet. For one brief moment, I had merged with the immense qi of the Supreme Peak master known as the Fire King Jeok Cheongang and felt it as my own.

[P104]
The root called the Fire Gate Clan. The trunk of the great tree that had grown from it, and its countless branches. I had clearly witnessed a glimpse of an unimaginably distant realm.

[P105]
Insight came from experiences and circumstances like this.

[P106]
Just like now.

[P107]
*I’m finally starting to see the way forward.*

[P108]
I could see them—the steps leading to a higher realm.

[P109]
It was a small insight no one could have taught me.

[P110]
Chime.

[P111]
> **System**
> - The realm of **Fire Gate Divine Technique** has risen to seven stars!
> - You can manipulate, release, and withdraw qi more freely!
> - You can now perform the martial arts of the **Fire Gate Clan** with greater power and effectiveness!
> - You have acquired a large amount of EXP and Bonus Points as a reward for your enlightenment!
> - Level Up!

[P112]
Yes. This was it.

[P113]
I opened my eyes to the cheerful chime. I had climbed only a single step, but the difference was immense.

[P114]
Through my newly sharpened senses, information about everything around me came flooding in.

[P115]
My entire body was drenched in sweat. The impurities I had expelled reeked. And someone was struggling silently behind me.

[P116]
“……”

[P117]
What the fuck?

[P118]
I turned my head and saw Cheongpung wrapped around Hyuk Mujin’s entire body like an anaconda, both hands clamped firmly over Mujin’s mouth and nose.

[P119]
“What are you doing over there?”

[P120]
Cheongpung answered brightly.

[P121]
“Hyuk Mujin was about to snore, so I was stopping him!”

[P122]
“Ah, well done. That bastard nearly pissed me off so badly I fell into qi deviation.”

[P123]
I told that idiot Hyuk Mujin to stand guard, and he was off dreaming the Butterfly Dream.[^1]

[P124]
I stared at Hyuk Mujin, whose face had turned blue as he struggled, and suddenly thought of something.

[P125]
“You only need to cover his nose. Why are you covering his mouth too?”

[P126]
“When I covered his nose, sounds started coming out of his mouth!”

[P127]
“Oh.”

[P128]
“So I covered both!”

[P129]
“Hmm. Won’t he suffocate and die?”

[P130]
“He can use the Turtle Breath Technique!”

[P131]
“What exactly is this damn Turtle Breath Technique?”

[P132]
“You hold your breath, stop your heartbeat, and lower your body temperature at the same time!”

[P133]
“Sounds incredible. Is that even possible?”

[P134]
“Of course. That’s what Hyuk Mujin is doing right now!”

[P135]
“Mujin is?”

[P136]
“Yes! His heartbeat has already stopped.”

[P137]
“……?”

[P138]
My brain stopped working.

[P139]
I stared silently at Hyuk Mujin. While we had been talking, he had stopped struggling, and his limbs now hung limp.

[P140]
“Gasp! Mujin!”

[P141]
“He’ll be cold soon!”

[P142]
“Get your hands off him right now, you lunatic!”

[P143]
“Huh? Maybe it isn’t the Turtle Breath Technique. Young Hero Hyuk? Can’t you hear me? Young Hero Hyuk?”

[P144]
I didn’t know about the Turtle Breath Technique, but the Ghost Technique certainly seemed accurate.

[P145]
Just before Hyuk Mujin could achieve Great Completion in the Ghost Technique, I slammed a palm into his chest.

[P146]
“Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Fist!”

[P147]
Thud!

[P148]
With the dull impact, a harsh breath burst from Hyuk Mujin’s open mouth.

[P149]
“Gahk!”

[P150]
“Oh no, Mujin! My left pinky!”

[P151]
“Cough, cough! C-Captain?”

[P152]
“Are you all right? Can you breathe?”

[P153]
“What?”

[P154]
Hyuk Mujin looked around in confusion. Maybe because he had been attacked in the middle of his sleep, he didn’t seem to understand what had happened.

[P155]
“What’s going on? I was just on a cloud.”

[P156]
“A cloud?”

[P157]
This idiot had really almost died.

[P158]
I was letting out a sigh of relief when Hyuk Mujin continued.

[P159]
“A man in white came over and started saying strange things. Something about a little lamb having come.”

[P160]
“What kind of lamb?”

[P161]
“A little lamb. Then he tried to embrace me, but there were holes this big in both his palms. I was about to cut him down without mercy when I woke up.”

[P162]
“……”

[P163]
Why was He showing up there?

[P164]
Just as I found myself at a loss for words, the door to our private room at Xi’an Tower slid open, and a grimy face poked inside.

[P165]
Gung Gibang looked over the dejected Cheongpung, Hyuk Mujin, who had just returned from the dead, and finally me, still shell-shocked.

[P166]
Then he muttered, “What a kennel.”

[P167]
Being treated like a dog by a beggar left a bad taste in my mouth.

[P168]
After barely pulling myself together, I asked Gung Gibang, “Were you out begging?”

[P169]
Gung Gibang shouted indignantly, “What are you talking about? I’m on my way back from our sect’s Xi’an branch!”

[P170]
The previous night, I had decided to spend a day at Xi’an Tower and recover from the fatigue of our journey. I had also asked Gung Gibang to gather information, so he must have visited the Xi’an branch for that reason.

[P171]
Since beggars were scattered throughout the world, the Beggars’ Sect had branches everywhere.

[P172]
In terms of sheer numbers, it was the greatest sect under heaven.

[P173]
“So? Did you find anything useful? Something about the Divine Physician’s whereabouts, for example.”

[P174]
“I did. Though it wasn’t about the Divine Physician.”

[P175]
Gung Gibang thought for a moment before continuing.

[P176]
“This information reeks to high heaven.”

[P177]
“More than you?”

[P178]
“……”

[P179]
“Sorry. Tell me.”

[P180]
Deeply offended, Gung Gibang refused to open his mouth until I had given him five silver nyang in alms.[^2]

[P181]
[^1]: A reference to Zhuangzi’s famous dream of becoming a butterfly.

[P182]
[^2]: A traditional silver currency unit.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 315

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃315화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|저벅, 저벅.
  6|
  7|종남일룡 혁소평의 발걸음은 빠르지도, 느리지도 않았다.
  8|
  9|그가 걸음을 내디딜 때마다 사람들의 시선과 수군거림이 따라붙었다.
 10|
 11|“쯧쯧, 대낮부터 이런 난동을 피우다니.”
 12|
 13|“문파 제일의 후기지수라는 자가 저 모양이니, 종남파 수준도 알 만해. 이러니 화산파가 늘 섬서 제일인 게지.”
 14|
 15|“볼은 왜 저렇게 부어 있대? 듣자 하니 화산일학이 왔다던데, 혹시…….”
 16|
 17|혁소평은 자신도 모르게 뺨을 문질렀다.
 18|
 19|욱신거리는 통증은 사람들의 따가운 시선 때문만이 아니다. 무기력하게 얻어맞은 세 대의 따귀. 그리고 한 사람의 가라앉은 목소리가 생생하게 떠올랐다.
 20|
 21|
 22|
 23|‘말했던 것 같은데. 그 검, 잘 생각하고 휘두르라고.’
 24|
 25|
 26|
 27|화왕 적천강이 선택한 열화문의 후인, 산서성이라는 작은 개천에서 몸을 일으킨 잠룡(潛龍).
 28|
 29|놈에 관한 이야기는 이미 지긋지긋할 정도로 들었다.
 30|
 31|하지만…….
 32|
 33|‘어떻게 그리 강할 수 있지?’
 34|
 35|도무지 이해할 수 없었다. 종남파 장문인의 적전제자로 들어가 전폭적인 지원 아래 무공을 익힌 그다.
 36|
 37|수많은 절정 무공과 영약, 십봉룡이라는 이름도 혁소평에게는 당연한 것이었다.
 38|
 39|그러나 지금, 혁소평을 둘러싼 것들이 위태롭게 흔들리고 있었다.
 40|
 41|입구에서 맞닥트린 서안루 총관의 차가운 표정은 그 증거 중 하나였다.
 42|
 43|“또 난동을 피우셨다고 들었습니다.”
 44|
 45|“난동? 약간 소란이 있긴 했지. 별일 아니니 넘어가자고.”
 46|
 47|그대로 지나치려는 혁소평의 발걸음은 다음 순간 들려온 총관의 말에 우뚝 멈췄다.
 48|
 49|“지난번에 말씀드렸었지요. 다시 한번 이런 일이 일어난다면 종남파에 정식으로 항의하겠다고요.”
 50|
 51|“항의?”
 52|
 53|번들거리는 눈빛으로 총관을 노려보던 혁소평이 입을 열었다.
 54|
 55|“우리 송 총관, 많이 컸네.”
 56|
 57|“혁 소협!”
 58|
 59|“건방 떨지 마.”
 60|
 61|혁소평의 잇새로 으르렁거리는 소리가 흘러나왔다.
 62|
 63|“루주 자식놈을 화산파 속가로 넣었다고 어깨가 올라간 모양인데…… 대종남파가 그리 우습게 보이나?”
 64|
 65|“말씀이 과하시군요.”
 66|
 67|총관의 딱딱하게 굳은 얼굴에 혁소평이 입매를 비틀었다.
 68|
 69|“과한 건 네놈들이야. 술이나 파는 놈들이 감히 본문을 우습게 보다니, 간이 배 밖으로 튀어나와도 유분수지.”
 70|
 71|“그 말씀, 루주께 그대로 전해 드려도 되겠습니까?”
 72|
 73|“잊지 말고 꼭 전해. 그럼 다음에 또 보자고.”
 74|
 75|툭툭.
 76|
 77|총관의 어깨를 두드리고 걸음을 옮기는 혁소평의 입가에는 씁쓸한 웃음이 맺혀 있었다.
 78|
 79|‘이제는 하다 하다 이런 놈들에게까지 무시받을 줄이야.’
 80|
 81|물론 서안루주는 일개 장사치라고 하기에는 그 영향력이 상당했다. 섬서성의 성도인 서안. 바로 그 서안의 유흥가를 주무르는 큰손이니까.
 82|
 83|그러나 제아무리 상계(商界)의 실력자라고 해도 구파일방의 이름 앞에서는 태양 앞의 잔딧불에 불과하다.
 84|
 85|더군다나 루주도 아닌, 일개 주루의 총관에게 자신이 이런 수모를 당할 줄이야.
 86|
 87|‘갈수록 점입가경이로군.’
 88|
 89|불과 일이 년 사이 종남파의 위상은 추락을 거듭했다.
 90|
 91|그 효시(嚆矢)를 쏘아 올린 것은 수많은 이들이 지켜보는 앞에서 노호검객을 박살 낸 화왕 적천강이었고, 은거를 깬 검성 매종학과 화산신룡이라는 이름이 뒤를 이었다.
 92|
 93|어찌 한 산에 두 마리 호랑이가 있을 수 있겠는가.
 94|
 95|누군가는 강자가 되어야 하고, 누군가는 약자가 되어야 한다. 종남파의 역할은 후자였다.
 96|
 97|‘언제까지고 지금 같지는 않을 것이다.’
 98|
 99|주르륵.
100|
101|있는 힘껏 움켜쥔 주먹에서 핏줄기가 흘렀다.
102|
103|지난밤부터 쌓여 있던 주독(酒毒)은 몰아낸 지 오래. 혁소평이 굳은 얼굴로 하늘을 바라보던 그때였다.
104|
105|“헉, 허억. 대사형, 여기 계셨군요.”
106|
107|“넌…… 봉수가 아니냐?”
108|
109|혁소평이 뜻밖이라는 눈빛으로 낯익은 얼굴을 바라봤다.
110|
111|거친 숨을 몰아쉬는 청년. 그는 혁소평과 같은 종남파의 제자로, 비록 사부는 다르나 항렬은 같았다.
112|
113|“본산에 있어야 할 네가 여기에는 어쩐 일이지?”
114|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
